Veterinary technician here! Ten years total, 5 years working in large animal hospital emergency rooms. Trained in animal CPR. Two things wrong with this video, I don't know what this man thought he was doing but it wasn't CPR, and I don't know how the dog was "resuscitated" but it more than likely had nothing to do with this man's actions.

1) His compressions were way, way, way too slow. There are two songs you can sing when doing doggy chest compressions, to keep the beat - the preferred one is obviously Stayin' Alive, but Another One Bites the Dust also works (discouraged). Tap your foot to the beat of those songs. That's how fast you need to pump a dog's heart to bring it out of arrest. This man was doing one compression every 2 or 3 seconds, he should have been doing 3 or 4 compressions per second.

2) His compressions were way, way, way too shallow. You need to compress the chest at least 30%. If it feels like you're pushing too hard, you're doing it right. That's how hard you need to push to force blood through the heart. In humans, it's not uncommon to break ribs during compressions. This man was feather-touching the dog's chest. That's not going to do anything.

Bonus 3) Blowing in a dog's nose does nothing.

So, what this man was doing was not animal CPR, please watch a video from a trained veterinarian before attempting CPR. Also remember, sadly, there is about a 5% chance of resuscitating an animal without all the other equipment we use in the ER.
